content: Oral contraceptives are medications that are administered orally with the primary purpose of preventing pregnancy. There are two main types of oral contraceptive pills available for females: 1. The combined oral contraceptive pill contains both oestrogen and a progestogen. It is taken once daily. 2. The progestogen-only pill, also known as the mini-pill, contains only a progestogen and is also taken once daily. In addition to these, there are other types of female oral contraceptives that are either experimental or available only in specific regions: Mifepristone, an antiprogestogen, has been studied as a daily oral contraceptive in clinical trials. Ormeloxifene, also known as Centchroman, is a selective oestrogen receptor modulator. It is taken one to two times per week and is approved as an oral contraceptive exclusively in India. Currently, there are no oral contraceptives available for males. However, several potential male contraceptive options are under various stages of research and development.
